# Implementation Plan: Plan 09 — MCP server at `tools/overview-mcp/`

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph --improve` on 2026-05-20. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/ralph-pipeline-09-mcp/plan.md`.*

**Worktree:** `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan` creates the worktree at `D:\harness-efforts\codexu\.ralph\jobs\ralph-pipeline-09-mcp\worktree\` on branch `ralph-pipeline-09-mcp`. All file edits in this plan happen in that worktree; commits land on the branch and are merged to `main` after Phase 6 review converges. Do NOT edit `main` directly. MCP server registration in `.claude/settings.local.json` is per-machine and gitignored — the implementer documents the registration step in the README but does NOT commit the settings change.

**Position in DAG:** depends on Plan 05 (snapshot input + schema), Plan 06 (next-command derivation), Plan 08 (crews integration for `invoke_next viaCrewMember` and `list_crew_sessions`). Plans 01–08 + 10 ship on `main` at HEAD `8de22837`. Plan 09 is the agent-facing programmatic mirror of the skill-driven UX (Plan 06).

## Overview

Plans 01–08 produce file-based interfaces (sidecar, snapshot, activity log, journal, recommendations). Agents can consume those by reading files, but that surface is brittle (path-typing, schema drift, no validation). This plan adds a first-class MCP server at `tools/overview-mcp/` exposing **10 typed tools** so other agents (the bookkeeping lead, any tool-using Claude Code session) call typed RPC instead of parsing files. Skills (Plan 06) remain the user-facing surface; MCP is the agent-to-agent / programmatic surface.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context

- **TypeScript types** live in `tools/overview-viewer/src/types.ts` — `Snapshot`, `SnapshotTask`, `RalphPipelineState`, `RalphStage`, `CrewSessionRef`, `Recommendation`, `NextCommand`, `DependencyGraph`, `OverviewData`, `OverviewTask`. The MCP server may use **type-only imports** from this file (zero runtime dependency, erased at compile time). The "don't import overview-viewer" rule in the Common Mistakes section is about React/Vite runtime code, not types.
- **Single-source shared libraries** in `scripts/lib/` consumed by the MCP server (each has an adjacent `.d.mts`):
  - `derive-next-command.mjs` — `deriveNextCommand(state, task, { repoRoot? }) → NextCommand | null`
  - `derive-next-command-cli.mjs` — CLI used inside `runWorkOnViaCrew()`
  - `append-journal.mjs` — currently only stage-transition lines; **must be additively extended** (see Story US-005)
  - `crews-cross-walk.mjs` — `discoverCrewSessions({ repoRoot, ralphState, overviewData, crewsRoot, now, logger })`
  - `parse-spawn-launcher.mjs` — `parseSpawnLauncher(absolutePath) → { initialPrompt, memberName, crewName }`
  - `work-on-via-crew.mjs` — `runWorkOnViaCrew({ repoRoot, config, taskId, stage, crewName, ... })`. **Lacks `.d.mts`** — Story US-001 adds one.
  - `sync-core.mjs` — exports `loadOverviewData(dataFile)`, `atomicWriteFile`. `loadOverviewData` is the trusted parser for `overview-data.js`.
  - `resolve-config.mjs` — resolves `repoRoot`, `config.dataFile`, `config.outputs.{snapshot,snapshotSchema,recommendationsJson,dependencyGraphJson,...}`, `config.crewsRoot`, `config.lockFile`. **Use this — do not hardcode `plans/*` paths.**
  - `atomic-write.mjs` — `atomicWriteFile(filePath, contents)` (tmp + rename).
- **Snapshot artifact state:** at HEAD, `plans/overview-snapshot.json`, `plans/overview-snapshot.schema.json`, `plans/overview-recommendations.json`, `plans/overview-dependency-graph.json` are **not present on disk** — they are generated at runtime by `scripts/lib/watch-ralph-state.mjs` (started inside `pnpm overview` or `pnpm sync-ralph-state:watch`). The MCP server handles "snapshot missing" gracefully (clear error returned to the caller). Use `loadOverviewData()` to read `plans/overview-data.js` as a fallback data source for fields the snapshot doesn't carry (e.g. `workstream` map).
- **Reference MCP servers:**
  - **Primary:** `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/agent-peers/src/server.ts` + `index.ts` — uses `McpServer` from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js`, `zod` for input schemas, `server.tool(name, description, schema, handler)`, returns `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text }] }`. Stdio transport wired in `index.ts`.
  - **Secondary:** `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/happyMcpStdioBridge.ts` (in-repo stdio bridge).
- **Crews manifests:** `.crews/crews/<crewName>/{members,leads}/<name>/manifest.json` — fields `{ name, crew, role, sessionId, cwd, stateCwd, startedAt, lastHeartbeatAt, lastSummary, transcriptPath, listenerState, actorState }`. `list_crew_sessions` re-reads these on every call (cached ~500 ms).

### Technical Constraints

- **Module system:** ESM. `"type": "module"` in `package.json`. TypeScript emits `dist/` via `tsc -p tsconfig.json`. `target: ES2022`, `module: NodeNext`, `moduleResolution: NodeNext`, `outDir: dist`.
- **Workspace registration is duplicated** in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` AND root `package.json.workspaces.packages`. Both must be updated (existing `tools/overview-viewer/CLAUDE.md` calls this out; same applies here).
- **Stdio MCP protocol** uses `stdout` for JSON-RPC traffic. **All diagnostic output must go to `stderr`** (use `console.error(...)` / a stderr logger; never `console.log`).
- **No new top-level dependencies in the workspace:** `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, `zod`, `@babel/parser` are all new and declared only in `tools/overview-mcp/package.json`. `chokidar` already exists as a root devDep (v5.0.0) but the package can declare its own to avoid version coupling.
- **Tests:** vitest (matches `tools/overview-viewer/`). Tests live in `tools/overview-mcp/src/__tests__/`. The root `vitest.config.ts` only matches `scripts/**/*.test.mjs`, so the new package owns its own `vitest.config.ts` and `pnpm --filter @codexu/overview-mcp test` runs them.
- **Windows host:** Verification commands must use PowerShell (`Get-Content -Tail`, `Get-FileHash`) — no bash-only `tail` / `head`.

`tools/overview-mcp/src/index.ts`:
```ts
#!/usr/bin/env node
import { StdioServerTransport } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/stdio.js'
import { createServer } from './server.js'
import { buildContext } from './context.js'

async function main() {
  const ctx = await buildContext()
  const server = await createServer(ctx)
  const transport = new StdioServerTransport()
  await server.connect(transport)
  process.stderr.write(`[overview-mcp] connected (repoRoot=${ctx.repoRoot})\n`)
}

main().catch((err) => {
  process.stderr.write(`[overview-mcp] fatal: ${err?.stack ?? err}\n`)
  process.exit(1)
})
```

## Tool implementation notes

### `overview.set_override` — structured edit strategy
Babel's `@babel/generator` reformats source even with `retainLines + compact: false`, so the byte-identity acceptance criterion is incompatible with regenerating the whole file. Use **AST locate + source-string splice**:

1. Read `plans/overview-data.js` as a string.
2. Parse with `@babel/parser` (`sourceType: 'script'`, `errorRecovery: true`). Locate the `window.OVERVIEW_DATA = <ObjectExpression>` assignment.
3. Walk the ObjectExpression's properties looking for `ralphOverrides`. Two cases:
   - **Exists:** record the value node's `[start, end]` offsets. Build the replacement string by `JSON.stringify(newOverrides, null, 4)` and re-indent to match the surrounding indentation. Splice.
   - **Absent:** locate the `tasks:` property's `[end]` offset. Build the insertion string (newline + indent + `"ralphOverrides": {...},` + matching trailing comma adjustment). Splice immediately after the `tasks` property's trailing comma.
4. Validate the resulting string parses cleanly via `@babel/parser` (defensive — if parse fails, return `{ ok: false, error }` and do NOT write).
5. Write atomically via `atomicWriteFile()` from `scripts/lib/atomic-write.mjs`.

**Locking:** `set_override` does NOT acquire `.ralph/overview-sync.lock`. That lock is for snapshot generation; grabbing it from a fast structured-edit would block snapshot writers unnecessarily. The atomic rename gives readers a coherent file at all times. Document this choice in the tool's docstring.

### `overview.invoke_next` — two modes
- **Default (no `viaCrewMember`):** the MCP server runs as a stdio subprocess and cannot invoke a Claude Code Skill. Return `{ ok: true, command: <NextCommand>, invocationGuidance: 'use the Skill tool to invoke this — for example: Skill("ralph-orchestration:run-ralph", args="...")' }`. The caller agent then invokes the skill itself.
- **`viaCrewMember`:** delegate entirely to `runWorkOnViaCrew({ repoRoot, config, taskId, stage: ralph.stage, crewName, memberName?, stdout: process.stderr })` from `scripts/lib/work-on-via-crew.mjs`. That helper preflights the watcher lock, derives the prompt via the next-command CLI, spawns through `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tools/spawn-member.js`, polls the member manifest for `sessionId`+`transcriptPath`, and persists the ref via `scripts/sync-ralph-state.mjs --update-crew-session`. Passing `stdout: process.stderr` is required because the helper writes a `Spawned <crew>/<member>...` confirmation line and the MCP server reserves stdout for JSON-RPC. The MCP tool returns the resulting `sessionRef`.
- **Without Plan 08 shipped:** `runWorkOnViaCrew()` exists post-Plan 08 and is required. If `scripts/lib/work-on-via-crew.mjs` is missing, the tool returns `{ ok: false, error }` with a clear message.

### `overview.list_crew_sessions` — live re-read
Reuse `discoverCrewSessions({ repoRoot, ralphState, overviewData, crewsRoot, now })` from `scripts/lib/crews-cross-walk.mjs` for task/stage matching, but do not return its `CrewSessionRef` values directly: `CrewSessionRef` intentionally does not include live manifest fields such as `lastHeartbeatAt`. Define an MCP-package-local `LiveCrewSession` response shape in `tools/overview-mcp/src/tools/list-crew-sessions.ts` that starts from the discovered session ref and adds `lastHeartbeatAt`, `lastSummary`, `lastTurnAt`, `listenerState`, and `actorState` from a fresh manifest read. Resolve `.crews/` through `config.crewsRoot` so linked worktrees read the main repo's shared crew state, and re-open the matching `.crews/crews/<crewName>/{members,leads}/<memberName>/manifest.json` (matching by `sessionId` when available) immediately before returning. Build the inputs from the SnapshotReader's cached `ralphState` (or read `plans/overview-ralph-state.json` directly if snapshot is missing). Cache the discovery + manifest merge for 500 ms per call site to avoid hammering the FS. If `taskId` is provided, filter by `matchTaskId()` post-discovery.

### `overview.get_transcript` — JSONL reverse-tail
Resolve `sessionId → transcriptPath` by scanning `.crews/.../manifest.json` files (or look up via cached `discoverCrewSessions()` result). Then tail the JSONL: use a backward chunk read (read last 64 KB; if fewer than `lastN` complete lines, read the previous 64 KB; repeat to a max file size). Parse each line as a Claude Code transcript entry. Skip the final non-empty line if it fails to parse (torn-write tolerance — same pattern as `useActivityEvents()` in overview-viewer). By default filter `tool_use` / `tool_result` entries; include them when `includeToolEvents: true`. Cap default `lastN` at 100 to keep response size bounded.

### `overview.add_journal_entry` — new helper
The plan contract is `{ taskId, note }`, but the existing `appendJournalEntry()` only formats stage transitions. **Resolution:** extend `scripts/lib/append-journal.mjs` additively with a new export:
```js
export function appendJournalNote({ repoRoot, taskId, ts, note }) { /* fsync append */ }
```
Format: `- <ts>  note: <single-line>\n`. Multi-line notes get `\n  ` continuation indent (each subsequent line indented two spaces under the first). Add `appendJournalNote` to `scripts/lib/append-journal.d.mts`. The existing `appendJournalEntry()` remains unchanged — bookkeeper code that writes stage transitions keeps working unchanged.

### `SnapshotReader` — single cache, chokidar invalidation
```ts
class SnapshotReader {
  private snapshot: Snapshot | null = null
  private snapshotMtime: number | null = null
  private overviewData: OverviewData | null = null
  private overviewDataMtime: number | null = null
  private watcher: chokidar.FSWatcher | null = null

  async getSnapshot(): Promise<Snapshot | null> { /* lazy read + cache */ }
  async getOverviewData(): Promise<OverviewData> { /* lazy read via loadOverviewData() + cache */ }
  start(): void { /* chokidar.watch(config.outputs.snapshot, config.dataFile) — invalidate caches on change */ }
  async close(): Promise<void> { /* watcher.close() */ }
}
```
chokidar fires on writes; the reader nulls its cache and re-reads lazily. No additional polling. Tolerates missing files (`getSnapshot()` returns `null` when the file doesn't exist).

### MCP install script (`install-server.ts`)
CLI behavior (`pnpm overview-mcp:install`):
1. Compute absolute path `<repoRoot>/tools/overview-mcp/dist/index.js`. Convert to forward slashes; assert `dist/index.js` exists (else error: "run `pnpm overview-mcp:build` first").
2. Read `.claude/settings.local.json` (create `{}` if absent).
3. Merge under `mcpServers.codexu-overview`:
   ```json
   { "command": "node", "args": ["<absolute-path-to-dist/index.js>"] }
   ```
4. Write atomically via `atomicWriteFile()`.
5. Print a summary block to stdout. Accepts `--print-only` to emit the JSON to stdout without writing.

## Risk Areas

- **`set_override` byte-identity** — the highest-risk surface. Mitigation: AST-locate + source-splice (do NOT use babel-generator). Tests assert that the file differs ONLY in the spliced byte range; fuzz the insertion case with multiple placements.
- **Snapshot file may be absent at runtime** — Plan 05's watcher must be running for the snapshot to exist. Read tools return clear errors when snapshot is missing; document the dependency in README ("`pnpm overview` or `pnpm sync-ralph-state:watch` must be running for full functionality").
- **`appendJournalEntry` contract mismatch** — addressed by additive extension (new `appendJournalNote` export). Tests verify the existing function is unchanged.
- **Chokidar torn-read race** — if chokidar fires while a write is in progress, reader may attempt to parse a partial file. Mitigation: wrap parse in try/catch; on parse failure, schedule a 100 ms retry and re-read; if still failing after 3 retries, return cached value or null.
- **`runWorkOnViaCrew()` lacks a `.d.mts`** — adding one is a small, low-risk change but lives in `scripts/lib/`, which is shared infrastructure. Tests in `scripts/lib/work-on-via-crew.test.mjs` already cover the behavior; the new `.d.mts` is type-only.
- **Stdout pollution** — stdio MCP uses stdout for JSON-RPC. Any accidental `console.log` from a tool handler corrupts the protocol stream. Mitigation: lint rule disabled? No — instead, document in CLAUDE.md for the package and review handlers carefully. The Result helper enforces returning via the MCP `content` channel, not stdout.
- **Windows path handling** — `transcriptPath` is an absolute Windows path with backslashes. The transcript reader must handle both `\` and `/` separators; the install script writes forward-slash paths into the settings JSON (Claude Code normalizes either, but forward slashes are more portable).

Apply updates atomically; in the commit message, list each diff so reviewers can verify the cascade.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

### US-001: Scaffold package + shared TypeScript context
**Description:** As an implementer, I want a working `tools/overview-mcp/` package with all build infrastructure so subsequent stories can implement tools.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `tools/overview-mcp/package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, `README.md` (stub), `src/index.ts` (skeleton entrypoint), `src/server.ts` (empty `createServer`), `src/context.ts` (`buildContext()` returns `{ repoRoot, config }` via `resolve-config.mjs`).
- [ ] `pnpm-workspace.yaml` includes `tools/overview-mcp`.
- [ ] Root `package.json` includes `tools/overview-mcp` in `workspaces.packages` and adds `overview-mcp:build` and `overview-mcp:install` scripts.
- [ ] `scripts/lib/work-on-via-crew.d.mts` exists with `runWorkOnViaCrew` declared (type-only, mirroring the JS).
- [ ] `pnpm install` updates `pnpm-lock.yaml`; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds; `pnpm --filter @codexu/overview-mcp build` produces `dist/index.js`; `pnpm --filter @codexu/overview-mcp typecheck` passes.
- [ ] Server starts (`node dist/index.js`) without crashing and logs `connected` to stderr, then exits cleanly on SIGINT.
**Dependencies:** None
**Estimated complexity:** small

### US-002: SnapshotReader + ServerContext (lazy load + chokidar invalidation)
**Description:** As a tool implementer, I want a `SnapshotReader` that lazily loads `Snapshot` and `OverviewData` from disk and invalidates on file change, so every read-only tool shares one cached parse path.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `SnapshotReader` class with `getSnapshot()`, `getOverviewData()`, `start()`, `close()`.
- [ ] Uses `chokidar.watch()` on `config.outputs.snapshot` and `config.dataFile`. On change, nulls caches; next `get*()` re-reads.
- [ ] Returns `null` when snapshot file is missing (no throw).
- [ ] `getOverviewData()` reuses `loadOverviewData()` from `scripts/lib/sync-core.mjs`.
- [ ] Tests: fixture under `tmp/`, write snapshot → read → modify → read → assert refreshed; verify torn-write tolerance.
**Dependencies:** US-001
**Estimated complexity:** medium

### US-003: Read-only snapshot tools — `list_tasks`, `get_task`, `next_command`, `list_recommendations`, `list_blockers`
**Description:** As an agent, I want the five read-only tools so I can introspect the pipeline without parsing files.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] All five tools registered with zod input schemas in `src/schemas.ts`.
- [ ] `list_tasks` supports filters: `stage`, `scope`, `workstream` (looked up via `OverviewData.workstream`), `hasDeferredQuestions`, `hasOpenFindings`. Title falls back to `command.descriptionHtml` plaintext or `command.name`.
- [ ] `get_task` validates `taskId` with `assertSafeTaskId` from `scripts/lib/append-journal.mjs` before reading `tasks/<taskId>/journal.md`; invalid ids return `{ ok: false, error }` and perform no filesystem read.
- [ ] `get_task` returns merged `SnapshotTask` + `recentJournal: string[]` (last 3 lines of `tasks/<taskId>/journal.md`).
- [ ] `next_command` calls `deriveNextCommand()` directly; result matches `node scripts/lib/derive-next-command-cli.mjs <taskId>`.
- [ ] `list_recommendations` reads `snapshot.recommendations`; falls back to `plans/overview-recommendations.json`; both missing → `{ ok: false, error }`. Supports `limit` and `stageFilter`.
- [ ] `list_blockers` returns tasks where `stage === 'blocked'` OR `Object.values(reviewOpenCount ?? {}).some((n) => (n ?? 0) > 0)` OR `(deferredQuestionsCount ?? 0) > 0`.
- [ ] One test per tool, happy path + at least one error / missing-snapshot case.
- [ ] Typecheck passes; per-tool vitest tests pass.
**Dependencies:** US-002
**Estimated complexity:** medium

### US-004: `add_journal_entry` + `appendJournalNote()` helper
**Description:** As an agent, I want to append a free-form note to a task's journal so I can record context without going through the bookkeeper.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `scripts/lib/append-journal.mjs` exports the existing `assertSafeTaskId(taskId)` guard and adds `appendJournalNote({ repoRoot, taskId, ts, note })`. Format: `- <ts>  note: <note>\n` with `\n  ` continuation for multi-line notes.
- [ ] `scripts/lib/append-journal.d.mts` declares `appendJournalEntry`, `appendJournalNote`, and `assertSafeTaskId`.
- [ ] `scripts/lib/append-journal.test.mjs` extends with single-line, multi-line, and special-character cases; the existing stage-transition tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] MCP `overview.add_journal_entry` tool wraps `appendJournalNote()`. `ts` defaults to `new Date().toISOString()`.
- [ ] Reuses `assertSafeTaskId` (the existing taskId validator) — no path traversal possible.
- [ ] Tests verify atomic append (`fsync`) and idempotency.
**Dependencies:** US-001
**Estimated complexity:** small

### US-005: `set_override` (structured edit)
**Description:** As an agent, I want to set `ralphOverrides[slug] = taskId` in `plans/overview-data.js` without touching any other field.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `src/utils/set-override-edit.ts` exposes `editOverrides({ source, slug, taskId }): { source: string }` — pure function (no I/O).
- [ ] Uses `@babel/parser` only to LOCATE AST ranges; splices the original source string. Does NOT call `@babel/generator`.
- [ ] Handles both cases: `ralphOverrides` already present (replace value) or absent (insert after `tasks:`).
- [ ] Tool wrapper reads `config.dataFile`, calls `editOverrides`, validates result parses, writes via `atomicWriteFile()`.
- [ ] Returns `{ ok: false, error }` on parse failure or absent `window.OVERVIEW_DATA` assignment — does NOT overwrite.
- [ ] **Byte-range confinement test**: load a representative fixture (`fixtures/overview-data.sample.js`), edit, assert every byte outside the spliced range is unchanged. Run for: (a) override absent, (b) override present, (c) override present with the same value (no-op edit), (d) malformed source (asserts `{ ok: false }`).
- [ ] Per-tool vitest test passes.
**Dependencies:** US-002
**Estimated complexity:** large

### US-006: `list_crew_sessions` (live re-read with 500 ms cache)
**Description:** As an agent, I want to see live crew sessions per task (not the snapshot's cached view) so I can react to active members.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Reuses `discoverCrewSessions()` from `scripts/lib/crews-cross-walk.mjs` with fresh inputs (Ralph state + OverviewData + `config.crewsRoot`).
- [ ] Defines a local `LiveCrewSession` response type in `tools/overview-mcp/src/tools/list-crew-sessions.ts`; keep shared `CrewSessionRef` unchanged.
- [ ] After discovery, re-opens each matching manifest under `config.crewsRoot` and merges live fields into the response: `lastHeartbeatAt`, `lastSummary`, `lastTurnAt`, `listenerState`, and `actorState`.
- [ ] Caches the discovery result for 500 ms (a single `discoverCrewSessions()` call serves all reads within the window).
- [ ] Optional `taskId` filter — matches via the same heuristic as the cross-walk module.
- [ ] Live-read regression: test writes a manifest with `lastHeartbeatAt = T1`, calls the tool (returns T1), advances 600 ms, updates manifest to `T2`, calls again (returns T2).
**Dependencies:** US-002
**Estimated complexity:** medium

### US-007: `get_transcript` (JSONL reverse-tail with torn-line tolerance)
**Description:** As an agent, I want to read the tail of a session transcript by `sessionId` so I can review what another agent did.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `src/utils/transcript-tail.ts` exposes `tailTranscript({ transcriptPath, lastN, includeToolEvents }): Array<TranscriptTurn>`.
- [ ] Reads file backward in 64 KB chunks; stops when N complete lines collected or file exhausted; caps at 100 lastN.
- [ ] Tolerates a malformed final line (torn write) — skip without warning. Malformed interior lines log a stderr warning.
- [ ] Filters `tool_use` / `tool_result` entries by default; `includeToolEvents: true` retains them.
- [ ] Tool resolves `sessionId → transcriptPath` via cached `discoverCrewSessions()` result (or scans `.crews/.../manifest.json` directly).
- [ ] Test fixture: JSONL with 50 mixed entries; assert last 20 user/assistant turns by default; assert full set with `includeToolEvents`.
**Dependencies:** US-006
**Estimated complexity:** medium

### US-008: `invoke_next` (default + `viaCrewMember`)
**Description:** As an agent, I want one tool that either tells me the next command to run, or spawns a crew member to run it.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Default mode: calls `deriveNextCommand()`, returns `{ ok: true, command, invocationGuidance }`.
- [ ] `viaCrewMember` mode: delegates to `runWorkOnViaCrew({ repoRoot, config, taskId, stage, crewName, memberName?, stdout: process.stderr })` so the helper's spawn confirmation line goes to stderr, not the MCP JSON-RPC stdout channel. Returns `{ ok: true, sessionRef }`.
- [ ] If `scripts/lib/work-on-via-crew.mjs` is missing (Plan 08 not shipped), returns `{ ok: false, error: 'requires plan 08' }` — but at HEAD post-Plan 08, this path is active.
- [ ] Tests use mocks for `runWorkOnViaCrew()` and assert the call args; one end-to-end test with a temp `.crews/` fixture is optional but encouraged.
**Dependencies:** US-002, US-003
**Estimated complexity:** medium

### US-009: `install-server.ts` (`.claude/settings.local.json` patcher)
**Description:** As an operator, I want a one-command install that registers the MCP server in my machine-local settings.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] CLI binary `overview-mcp-install` (declared as `package.json.bin`).
- [ ] Reads `<repoRoot>/.claude/settings.local.json` (creates `{}` if absent).
- [ ] Merges under `mcpServers.codexu-overview`: `{ command: 'node', args: ['<absolute-path-to-dist/index.js>'] }`.
- [ ] Writes atomically via `atomicWriteFile()`.
- [ ] `--print-only` flag emits the JSON to stdout without writing.
- [ ] Errors clearly if `dist/index.js` is absent (asks user to run `pnpm overview-mcp:build` first).
- [ ] Test uses a temp dir as repoRoot; asserts the file content after install.
**Dependencies:** US-001
**Estimated complexity:** small

### US-010: README + final INDEX refresh + downstream-plan audit
**Description:** As a future maintainer, I want clear docs on installation, registration, and each tool's contract; and the project INDEX must reflect the new package.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `tools/overview-mcp/README.md` covers: install (`pnpm overview-mcp:build && pnpm overview-mcp:install`); registration JSON layout; verifying with `/mcp` (or the Claude Code tool list); per-tool contract (name, inputs, outputs, mutation behavior, error envelope); Windows-specific PowerShell verification commands.
- [ ] `plans/ralph-pipeline-INDEX.md`: Source-of-truth modules table lists `tools/overview-mcp/` and the new `appendJournalNote` export; DAG diagram shows Plan 09 dependency edges.
- [ ] Any reference in `plans/ralph-pipeline-10-ralph-handoff.md` (if it mentions the MCP package) is updated.
- [ ] Atomic final commit; commit message lists each diff (file, lines, what changed) for reviewer auditability.
**Dependencies:** US-001..US-009
**Estimated complexity:** small

Shared touch on `src/server.ts` and `src/schemas.ts`. risk=medium (US-005 is the high-risk byte-identity edit; US-004 is small)

### Cluster: crew-tools

- `execution_mode` rationale: Serialize within this cluster (US-006 → US-007 → US-008) because US-007 reuses the cached discovery from US-006 and US-008 uses the same crew CLI surface. Could run in parallel after enabling the shared discovery cache in US-006.

- `execution_mode` rationale: Final cluster that consolidates docs + the INDEX refresh. Must run after all tools are stable so the README accurately documents them.

## Verification

A. **Workspace registration:** `pnpm install` from repo root updates `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds with the new package in the workspace.

B. **Build:** `pnpm overview-mcp:build` produces `tools/overview-mcp/dist/index.js`. PowerShell: `Test-Path tools/overview-mcp/dist/index.js`.

C. **Install:** `pnpm overview-mcp:install`. PowerShell: `Get-Content .claude/settings.local.json | ConvertFrom-Json | Select-Object -ExpandProperty mcpServers` — verify `codexu-overview` entry present.

D. **Tool discovery:** in Claude Code, run `/mcp` (if available) or check the tool list. Expect the 10 `overview.*` tools.

E. **`overview.list_tasks`:** invoke from Claude Code; returns the task list with stage labels.

F. **`overview.get_task`:** with a specific taskId; returns merged data + `recentJournal` (last 3 lines).

G. **`overview.next_command`:** call with a taskId; result matches `node scripts/lib/derive-next-command-cli.mjs <taskId>`.

H. **`overview.set_override`:** invoke with `{ slug: 'test-slug', taskId: 'test-task' }`. PowerShell: capture the pre/post hash of `plans/overview-data.js` via `Get-FileHash`; the diff is confined to the `ralphOverrides` byte range. `git diff plans/overview-data.js` should show only `ralphOverrides` additions/modifications.

I. **`overview.list_crew_sessions`:** with at least one active crew member running; returns sessions with live `lastHeartbeatAt` (not cached). Verify by updating a manifest's timestamp (e.g. via `(Get-Content manifest.json | ConvertFrom-Json) | ForEach-Object {...}`) and re-invoking the tool.

J. **`overview.get_transcript`:** with a valid `sessionId`; returns the last 20 turns; default-excludes tool events; `includeToolEvents: true` returns them.

K. **`overview.add_journal_entry`:** appends a line. PowerShell: `Get-Content tasks/<id>/journal.md -Tail 5` shows the new `- <ts>  note: ...` line.

L. **`overview.invoke_next` (default):** returns `{ ok: true, command, invocationGuidance }`. Caller side invocation via `Skill` is documented in README.

M. **`overview.invoke_next` (`viaCrewMember`):** with `crewName = ralph-pipeline`, spawns a crew member, polls manifest, returns `sessionRef` with `sessionId` and `transcriptPath` populated (or partial ref if poll times out).

N. **Test suite:** `pnpm --filter @codexu/overview-mcp test` passes. Existing `pnpm --filter @codexu/overview-viewer test` and `pnpm test:scripts` (or whatever the root suite is) pass — confirming no regression in the additive `append-journal.mjs` extension.

## Common mistakes / confusion points

1. **`set_override` writes a single field via AST locate + source-string splice.** NEVER call `@babel/generator` to serialize the whole file — the generator reformats. If the parser cannot find `window.OVERVIEW_DATA = {...}`, error gracefully (`{ ok: false, error }`) and tell the user to fix manually.
2. **MCP server runs as a stdio subprocess.** It cannot directly call Claude Code skills. `invoke_next` default mode returns the command; the caller invokes via the `Skill` tool itself.
3. **Live vs cached crew data.** `list_crew_sessions` re-reads manifests for live status; `get_task.ralph.crewSessions` is cached snapshot data (last tick's view). Each tool's docstring makes the distinction explicit.
4. **Settings.local.json, not settings.json.** Machine-specific paths shouldn't pollute committed config. `.claude/settings.local.json` is gitignored.
5. **Type-only imports from `tools/overview-viewer/src/types.ts` are allowed.** They are erased at compile time and create no runtime dependency. Do NOT import React, Vite, or any runtime exports from `tools/overview-viewer/`.
6. **`SnapshotReader` cache invalidation.** chokidar fires on writes; the reader nulls its cache and re-reads lazily. Don't add additional polling. Tolerate parse failures via a brief retry (mid-write torn reads).
7. **Keep TypeScript types and JSON Schema roles separate.** Import TypeScript shapes from `tools/overview-viewer/src/types.ts`; use `plans/overview-snapshot.schema.json` only for runtime JSON validation (optional in v1; can be added later).
8. **Backwards compatibility.** v1 tool contracts are committed once shipped. Adding a tool is non-breaking; changing an existing tool's input or output is breaking and requires a new tool or versioned variant.
9. **`invoke_next` with `viaCrewMember` delegates entirely to `runWorkOnViaCrew()`.** Do NOT reimplement spawn + poll + persist logic; reuse the shared helper at `scripts/lib/work-on-via-crew.mjs`. That helper already preflights `.ralph/overview-sync.lock` and refuses to spawn while the watcher holds it.
10. **`add_journal_entry` requires the new `appendJournalNote()` helper.** The existing `appendJournalEntry()` only formats stage transitions and must not be repurposed. Extend `scripts/lib/append-journal.mjs` additively; declare both functions in the new `.d.mts`.
11. **Path-traversal guard.** Every tool that builds a filesystem path from `taskId` must validate via `assertSafeTaskId` from `scripts/lib/append-journal.mjs` before touching the filesystem.
12. **All diagnostic output goes to stderr.** stdout is reserved for the MCP JSON-RPC protocol stream; a stray `console.log` corrupts the stream and breaks the client.
13. **Use `resolve-config.mjs` for paths.** Do not hardcode `plans/overview-snapshot.json` etc.; read them via `config.outputs.snapshot`, `config.dataFile`, `config.crewsRoot`, `config.lockFile`.
14. **Snapshot files may be absent.** The watcher must be running for snapshot artifacts to exist. Read tools return clear errors when missing — they do NOT crash the server.

## Open Questions

- **OQ-1 (deferred to implementer; resolved by recommendation):** `add_journal_entry { taskId, note }` contract mismatched `appendJournalEntry()`. Resolved by additively extending `scripts/lib/append-journal.mjs` with a new `appendJournalNote()` export (Story US-004). Confirmed safe — existing tests pass.
- **OQ-2 (deferred):** Should `overview.list_recommendations` re-score on the fly via `scoreRecommendations()` if the snapshot's recommendations array is stale (e.g. older than 5 min)? **v1 answer: no.** Snapshot freshness is the watcher's responsibility. Tool always prefers `snapshot.recommendations`, falls back to file. Re-scoring is a future enhancement.
- **OQ-3 (deferred):** Should the MCP server expose a `tools/call` over WebSocket transport in addition to stdio? **v1 answer: no.** Stdio is the standard MCP transport in Claude Code and `.claude/settings.local.json`. WebSocket is a future enhancement.
- **OQ-4 (deferred):** `overview.list_tasks workstream` filter requires loading `overview-data.js`. Decided to support it via `OverviewData.workstream` lookup; the SnapshotReader caches both `Snapshot` and `OverviewData`. If the keying of `workstream` in `overview-data.js` differs from what the planner assumed, the implementer adjusts the filter predicate during US-003 — fail soft (no workstream match → empty result, not an error).
- **OQ-5 (deferred):** Should `set_override` also remove a `slug → taskId` mapping when called with `taskId: null`? **v1 answer: no.** The tool only inserts/updates; deletion can ship as `unset_override` in v2 if requested.

### Open review findings (soft-capped at iteration 5+ — Medium-only state)

The plan-review convergence loop fixed all 6 High findings (F-001..F-006) across iterations 1–6 and soft-capped at iteration 7 with 8 Medium findings remaining open. These are quality clarifications, not blockers — implementation can proceed with the implementer applying these refinements inline as the relevant stories are reached.

- **F-007 (Medium, Feasibility — US-008):** `invoke_next` Plan-08-missing fallback only works with dynamic import. Use `const mod = await import('../../scripts/lib/work-on-via-crew.mjs').catch(() => null)` inside the handler; never a top-level static import. Defensive — Plan 08 has shipped.
- **F-008 (Medium, Simplicity — `list_crew_sessions`):** `matchTaskId()` is private in `scripts/lib/crews-cross-walk.mjs`. `discoverCrewSessions()` already returns a Map keyed by taskId — flatten and exact-filter; do not import the private helper.
- **F-009 (Medium, Criteria Quality — US-004):** Replace "idempotency" in the AC with concrete semantics: append is atomic (fsync), `tasks/<taskId>/` directory creation is idempotent via `fs.mkdirSync({ recursive: true })`, repeated identical calls append duplicate lines by design (no dedup), and existing stage-transition tests pass unchanged.
- **F-010 (Medium, Criteria Quality — US-008):** When `deriveNextCommand()` returns `null`, the tool returns `{ ok: true, command: null, invocationGuidance: 'no next command — task is complete or has no actionable next step' }`. Add to US-008 AC and the Tools table.
- **F-011 (Medium, Criteria Quality — US-006):** Tighten `list_crew_sessions` return type to `Array<{ taskId; stage; crewName; memberName; role; sessionId?; transcriptPath?; lastHeartbeatAt?; lastSummary?; lastTurnAt?; listenerState?; actorState? }>`. The live fields (everything past `transcriptPath`) come from re-reading the manifest file — see F-006's local `LiveCrewSession` type.
- **F-012 (Medium, Completeness — workspace registration AC):** Split the single workspace AC into three: (a) `pnpm-workspace.yaml` contains the entry; (b) root `package.json.workspaces.packages` contains the entry; (c) `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds in a clean checkout.
- **F-013 (Medium, Criteria Quality — US-004 regression):** Explicitly require `scripts/lib/append-journal.test.mjs` pre-existing stage-transition tests to pass unchanged alongside the new `appendJournalNote` tests.
- **F-014 (Medium, Criteria Quality — US-005 fixture):** Specify the fixture path `tools/overview-mcp/src/__tests__/fixtures/overview-data.sample.js` (representative `window.OVERVIEW_DATA` with ~5 tasks and the full top-level key set). Byte-range assertion: compare every byte outside the spliced `[start, end]` range via `Buffer.compare`. Four scenarios: insert, replace, no-op (same value), malformed source.
